title: Lightmap loads slower and uses more RAM in 4.6 compared to 4.5
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.6.1.stable.mono.official [14d19694e]
- Not reproducible in v4.5.1.stable.mono.official [f62fdbde1]

Also tested some of the 4.6 dev versions, but I'm not sure which ones i could actually reproduce it in, since it was a bit inconsistent. At one point it seemed like it started in 4.6 dev 4 and another time it seemed like it started in dev 5

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9174) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-8700 CPU @ 3.20GHz (12 threads) - 15.92 GiB memory

### Issue description

After upgrading my game from 4.5.1 to 4.6.1, I noticed it the RAM usage changed from about 500mb to 1150mb, and loading a save in my game went from about 1 second to 3-5 seconds. The editor also seems to use a lot more RAM, from around 1300mb to around 2000mb. I measured the RAM usage with task manager in windows.

I'm not sure if these are one or two different issues, but they seem related, since having my LightMapGI node hidden makes both issues disappear. When showing the LightMapGI node for the first time the memory usage increases and there is a lagspike. After it has been show initially the issue doesn't happen again when i return to the main menu and load the save/game world again in my game, but running the project again it always happens the first time.

I also noticed switching to directx12 doesn't have the memory issue, but the longer loading time still seems to happen, maybe even a bit longer. But my project uses vulkan.

### Steps to reproduce

The minimal reproduction project reproduces the issue for me, but a bit less than in my actual project, here it goes from around 500-600mb to 800mb, and the loading time is maybe from 1 second to 2 seconds.

How to reproduce:
- Open the project in godot 4.6.1 and bake the light map in test_scene.tscn
- Run the project
- Open task manager and expand the godot process to see the memory usage for the game, note how much it uses
- Press 'ui_left' to change from the empty main scene to the test scene with the lightmap
- Notice that the scene change takes around 2 seconds
- Notice that the memory usage in the task manager has increased by around 200mb
- Run the project and test again with godot 4.5.1
- Notice that the scene change is almost instant
- Notice that the memory usage only increased with 30-50mb

My numbers are from memory so they might be slightly wrong, but there should at least be a pretty noticable difference between godot 4.5.1 and godot 4.6.1.

Let me know if you need me to help test anything.
